Fake donations to charity involve creating fictitious records of contributions to legitimate or sham charitable organizations to claim tax deductions. This is a form of tax fraud, where you inflate or invent donation amounts on your tax return (e.g., via Schedule A of Form 1040 in the US) to reduce taxable income. The IRS allows deductions for qualified charitable contributions up to 60% of adjusted gross income (AGI) for cash donations, but only with proper substantiation. By fabricating evidence, you bypass verification to pocket the tax savings—essentially converting untaxed income into a "refund" via reduced liability.
